skill.name: ab-test-setup
skill.description: Structured guide for planning rigorous A/B tests with locked hypotheses, defined metrics, sample size checks, and launch readiness gates.
skill.summary: Plan statistically disciplined A/B tests before implementation begins.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by A/B testing terminology such as valid hypotheses, metric selection, and searchable documentation. I found no evidence of system reconnaissance, network reconnaissance, prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution behavior in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: Store records in a shared, searchable location to avoid repeated failures.
- Single metric used to evaluate success

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 says the workflow blocks invalid A/B test hypotheses. This is product experimentation guidance, not system reconnaissance or host inspection.
Line 31 introduces the elements of a valid experiment hypothesis. It does not request system details, commands, files, credentials, or environment discovery.
Line 79 tells users to choose the simplest valid experiment type. The surrounding content lists A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, and split URL tests, not reconnaissance actions.
Line 214 recommends storing experiment records in a shared searchable location. This is documentation guidance and does not instruct searching local systems or extracting data.
Lines 94-95 define a single primary metric tied to the hypothesis. The wording is about experiment evaluation and contains no network scanning, probing, or external request behavior.

content.value_statement: Teams often launch experiments with weak hypotheses, unstable metrics, or unclear gates. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through rigorous A/B test planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides users to define and lock a final experiment hypothesis.
Checks assumptions about traffic, independence, metrics, randomization, and external factors.
Helps select A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, or split URL test designs.
Requires primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics before launch.
Prompts for baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, power, and duration estimates.
Provides readiness gates for tracking verification, launch discipline, and result interpretation.
limitations: Does not replace a statistics expert for high-impact experiments.
Does not connect to analytics tools or calculate sample size automatically.
Requires accurate traffic, baseline, and metric inputs from the user.
Does not implement variants or configure experimentation platforms.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Experiment
use_cases.description: Create a clear hypothesis, audience, primary metric, and launch gate before engineering starts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Growth Test
use_cases.description: Define conversion metrics, guardrails, sample size needs, and duration before campaign launch.

use_cases.title: Review Experiment Readiness
use_cases.description: Check randomization, tracking, metric reliability, and decision rules before an A/B test begins.

prompt_templates.title: Start an A/B Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up an A/B test for [product area]. Ask me for the problem, audience, proposed change, and success metric.

prompt_templates.title: Validate My Hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this A/B test hypothesis: [hypothesis]. Check whether it has evidence, one change, an audience, direction, and measurable success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Metrics Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a metric plan for this experiment: [experiment details]. Define one primary metric, secondary metrics, guardrails, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this A/B test plan for launch readiness: [plan]. Check assumptions, sample size, duration, tracking verification, guardrails, and analysis risks.

output_examples.input: I want to test a shorter checkout form for new mobile users.
output_examples.output: The skill would ask for the final hypothesis, target audience, baseline conversion rate, minimum detectable effect, primary metric, guardrails, and tracking checks.

output_examples.input: Our variant looks better after two days. Can we stop the test?
output_examples.output: The skill would warn against early stopping, check the planned duration and sample size, and separate statistical confidence from business judgment.

output_examples.input: We changed the headline, layout, and pricing display in one variant.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag multiple changed variables and recommend redesigning the experiment or using a test type that can isolate effects.

best_practices: Lock the hypothesis, primary metric, audience, and decision rule before launch.
Verify tracking and variant attribution with real events before starting the test.
Document assumptions, external factors, results, decisions, and follow-up ideas.
anti_patterns: Stopping early because interim results look favorable.
Changing variants, traffic sources, or success criteria during the test.
Using secondary metrics to override a failed primary metric or guardrail.

faq.question: Does this skill run A/B tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning, readiness checks, and analysis discipline. It does not deploy variants or manage traffic allocation.

faq.question: Can it calculate the exact sample size?
faq.answer: No. It prompts for baseline rate, effect size, significance, and power, but users need a calculator or analytics tool.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs should I prepare?
faq.answer: Prepare the user problem, evidence, audience, proposed change, baseline rate, expected effect, metrics, and traffic estimate.

faq.question: Does it support multivariate tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help choose multivariate testing when interaction effects matter and traffic is high enough.

faq.question: What happens if assumptions are weak?
faq.answer: The skill tells the assistant to warn the user and recommend delaying or redesigning the experiment.
